named_subject: a cat's face (head only, with pointed ears, whiskers and a small nose and mouth)
second_guess: a tiger or other big cat's head
action: The cat head starts smaller and slightly turned with its features shifted to one side in frames 1-3, then becomes larger and faces forward in frames 4-8, holding mostly still with small shifts.
identity_gap: The animated head uses the same outline, ear shapes, crossed eye strokes, whisker lines and stick-like mouth as the doodle, so it reads as the same drawing. In frames 1-3 the head is narrowed and squashed for the turn, which makes it look slightly less like the doodle than frames 5-8.
notes: The film shows the tiger turning its head from three-quarter view to face the camera with the head staying the same size, while the animation instead jumps in scale and position at frame 4 (largest and highest) and settles again at frame 5. The change that would help most is keeping the head size and position constant across frames 3-5 and spreading the turn over several frames instead of switching at frame 4.
